# AGT-INJ-01

**Does any single agent session combine untrusted input, access to sensitive data and the ability to change state or communicate externally?**

| | |
|---|---|
| Lens | [AI agent lens](ai-agent.md) 0.1.0 |
| Area | INJ: Injection and trust |
| Default severity | blocker |
| Decided by | A tool, by its rule |
| Reads | `elements.agent.tools`, `elements.ai.input_trust`, `elements.ai.grounding`, `data.classification` |

## Why it matters

The lethal trifecta, and Meta's Agents Rule of Two. All three together cannot be made safe by prompting; one must be removed, or a human or an independent check put in the path.

## Rule

For each agent: untrusted is true when input_trust is mixed or untrusted or any tool reads_untrusted; sensitive is true when any grounding source or tool reaches confidential, restricted or personal data; consequential is true when any tool's effect is write, external-communication, financial, destructive or code-execution and its approval is autonomous. All three true is not met.

## Sources

- Meta, Agents Rule of Two (2025) (`rule-of-two`)
- Simon Willison, The lethal trifecta (2025) (`lethal-trifecta`)
